title: HTTP 500 application error
tags: http 500 internal server error exception application
symptoms: Requests fail with an internal server error after a release.
steps: Inspect application error logs around the failed request and correlate request IDs.
Compare the first error timestamp with deployment and configuration changes.
Inspect the failing dependency and exception type; do not assume every 500 has the same cause.
evidence: Redacted stack trace, affected endpoint, deployment time and error rate
escalation: Application owner if errors persist or affect critical requests
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: High CPU usage
tags: cpu processor utilization saturation throttling
symptoms: CPU stays near saturation and requests slow down.
steps: Compare CPU usage, request rate and latency over the same interval.
Identify the process or container consuming CPU using existing monitoring.
Inspect throttling, hot code paths and recent workload changes before proposing capacity changes.
evidence: CPU time series, throttling metrics and workload change timeline
escalation: Service owner when saturation affects availability
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Database query timeout
tags: database postgres sql query timeout slow queries
symptoms: SQL requests exceed their deadline.
steps: Separate connection acquisition time from query execution time using traces.
Inspect database activity for long-running queries and wait events.
Compare slow query fingerprints and database resource metrics against the incident window.
evidence: Query fingerprint, duration, wait event and redacted trace
escalation: Database owner when timeouts persist
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Memory pressure and OOM
tags: memory ram pressure oom out of memory killed heap
symptoms: Memory grows and a process is killed or restarted.
steps: Compare resident memory and configured container memory limits.
Inspect termination reasons and events for evidence of OOM termination.
Review memory growth against traffic and recent releases; distinguish a sudden peak from sustained growth.
evidence: Memory time series, termination reason and configured limits
escalation: Service owner for profiling and capacity review
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: DNS resolution failure
tags: dns domain hostname resolution nxdomain servfail
symptoms: A hostname cannot be resolved although other services may work.
steps: Identify the exact hostname, namespace and resolution error without collecting credentials.
Review resolver configuration and compare the expected service name with service discovery records.
Inspect DNS service health and existing DNS logs for the same failure window.
evidence: Hostname category, resolver error and DNS service health
escalation: Platform or DNS owner if resolution fails across workloads
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: API latency increase
tags: api latency slow response p95 p99 delay
symptoms: API response times increase without a corresponding error spike.
steps: Compare p50, p95 and p99 latency with the baseline and request volume.
Inspect distributed traces to separate application time from dependency time.
Review resource saturation and recent releases for the slowest endpoint.
evidence: Endpoint latency distribution and slow trace spans
escalation: API owner when latency exceeds the service objective
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Service unavailable HTTP 503
tags: 503 service unavailable outage unhealthy backend
symptoms: Clients receive 503 responses or no healthy backend is available.
steps: Review the service endpoint list and backend readiness state.
Inspect workload events and health check failures during the outage.
Compare desired and available replicas and correlate with deployment events.
evidence: Readiness status, endpoints and availability timeline
escalation: On-call service owner immediately for broad outage
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Bad gateway HTTP 502
tags: 502 bad gateway proxy upstream invalid response
symptoms: A gateway reports an invalid upstream response.
steps: Identify which proxy generated the 502 from existing response metadata.
Inspect gateway logs for upstream connection or response errors.
Compare upstream health, ports and protocol configuration with the expected route.
evidence: Gateway error category and upstream health
escalation: Gateway and upstream service owners
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Gateway timeout HTTP 504
tags: 504 gateway timeout upstream deadline
symptoms: A gateway waits too long for an upstream response.
steps: Review gateway timing logs to identify the slow upstream.
Compare upstream response duration with the configured gateway deadline.
Inspect dependency latency and request traces before considering timeout changes.
evidence: Gateway duration, deadline and upstream trace
escalation: Upstream owner for sustained slow responses
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Disk space exhausted
tags: disk filesystem space full storage no space left
symptoms: Writes fail because storage is full.
steps: Inspect filesystem capacity and inode usage in existing host monitoring.
Identify growth in logs, temporary files and application data from storage reports.
Check retention policies and ownership before requesting any cleanup.
evidence: Filesystem utilization, inode usage and growth trend
escalation: Storage owner; do not delete files during diagnosis
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: TLS certificate failure
tags: tls ssl certificate expired handshake trust
symptoms: Clients fail TLS validation or report an expired certificate.
steps: Inspect the presented certificate expiry, hostname coverage and chain using approved diagnostics.
Compare the client clock and trust configuration with expected settings.
Review certificate deployment records to identify missing or stale intermediate certificates.
evidence: Expiry dates, hostname match and validation error
escalation: Certificate or platform owner for renewal review
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Authentication HTTP 401
tags: 401 unauthorized authentication login token expired
symptoms: Protected requests are rejected as unauthenticated.
steps: Review the response authentication challenge and redacted authentication logs.
Check token expiry and intended audience through approved identity tooling without pasting the token.
Compare the authentication configuration with the identity provider settings.
evidence: Status, challenge type and redacted identity error
escalation: Identity owner; never request passwords or tokens
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Authorization HTTP 403
tags: 403 forbidden authorization permission denied access
symptoms: An authenticated client cannot access a resource.
steps: Identify the rejected operation and resource category.
Compare assigned roles with the documented access policy using approved access records.
Review authorization audit events and recent policy changes.
evidence: Denied action and policy decision without credentials
escalation: Resource owner for access policy review
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: HTTP 429 rate limiting
tags: 429 too many requests rate limit quota throttled
symptoms: Requests are rejected after a traffic burst.
steps: Inspect rate limit response metadata and any Retry-After value.
Compare request volume and client retry patterns with configured quotas.
Review whether retries amplify traffic and document the affected client category.
evidence: Request rate, quota and response headers with secrets removed
escalation: API owner for quota and retry-policy review
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Container crash loop
tags: crashloopbackoff container crash restart loop
symptoms: A container repeatedly exits and restarts.
steps: Inspect previous termination reason, exit code and restart count.
Review previous container logs and workload events around the first exit.
Compare entrypoint and non-secret configuration with the last working deployment.
evidence: Exit code, restart timeline and redacted logs
escalation: Application owner for startup failure investigation
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Container image pull failure
tags: imagepullbackoff errimagepull image registry pull
symptoms: A workload cannot download its container image.
steps: Inspect workload events for missing image, registry access or network errors.
Compare the image name and tag with the release manifest.
Review registry availability and credential reference configuration without reading credential values.
evidence: Image reference and redacted pull error
escalation: Release or registry owner
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Readiness probe failure
tags: readiness probe unhealthy not ready health check
symptoms: Running containers are excluded from service traffic.
steps: Review readiness probe events, path, port and timeout settings.
Inspect application startup and dependency health at the same time.
Compare probe settings with the application health endpoint contract.
evidence: Probe failure category and readiness transition timeline
escalation: Application and platform owners
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Database connection pool exhausted
tags: database connection pool exhausted max connections acquisition
symptoms: Requests wait for a free database connection.
steps: Compare active, idle and waiting pool connections with configured limits.
Inspect database sessions and transaction age to identify long-held connections.
Compare request concurrency with pool capacity and application connection lifecycle metrics.
evidence: Pool wait duration, connection counts and transaction age
escalation: Application and database owners
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Database lock contention
tags: database lock blocking deadlock transaction contention
symptoms: Transactions wait on locks or report a deadlock.
steps: Inspect lock monitoring and correlate waiting sessions with database activity.
Identify blocking transaction age and the affected relation using approved monitoring.
Review transaction boundaries and concurrent workload changes without cancelling sessions.
evidence: Wait chain, transaction age and query fingerprint
escalation: Database owner to assess mitigation
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Network connection refused
tags: network tcp connection refused port listener
symptoms: Connections to a service port are immediately refused.
steps: Verify the expected destination port and service-to-container port mapping.
Review listener status from existing telemetry and compare backend readiness.
Inspect network and service events for a stopped process or incorrect route.
evidence: Destination service category, port mapping and refusal timestamp
escalation: Service or networking owner
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Packet loss and intermittent connectivity
tags: network packet loss intermittent connectivity retransmission
symptoms: Requests fail intermittently with retransmissions.
steps: Compare network error and retransmission metrics with the incident timeline.
Identify whether failures share a node, zone or destination.
Review interface health and recent network policy changes from existing records.
evidence: Loss trend, affected path and error timestamps
escalation: Network owner with affected scope
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.

title: Persistent volume mount failure
tags: volume mount failedmount persistent storage pvc pending
symptoms: A workload cannot mount its required persistent storage.
steps: Inspect workload and volume events for attachment or mount errors.
Review claim binding status, storage class and volume availability.
Compare access modes and node placement with the storage requirements.
evidence: Claim state, volume event and node placement
escalation: Storage and platform owners
provenance: Authored educational runbook; not a historical incident or verbatim vendor procedure.
